module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 699

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/699](https://www.erdosproblems.com/699)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos699

/-- Sylvester and Schur: for $1 \le i \le n/2$ there is a prime $p > i$ dividing `n.choose i`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AllenGrahamHart/FormalConjectures-Bench/blob/482dacc4d9335240f26218cdc62032da3100392b/formalizations/erdos699/Erdos699Formalization.lean#L7679"]
theorem sylvester_schur (n i : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hi_half : i ≤ n / 2) :
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.choose n i := by
  sorry

/--
**Erdős Problem 699.** Is it true that for every $1 \le i < j \le n / 2$ there exists a prime
$p \ge i$ with $p \mid \gcd\big(\binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j}\big)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_699 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n i j : ℕ,
      1 ≤ i →
      i < j →
      j ≤ n / 2 →
      ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that, apart from a finite exceptional set of triples `(n, i, j)`,
one can always take `p > i` in the prime divisor statement. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_szekeres_strengthening : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ E : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ), ∀ n i j : ℕ,
      1 ≤ i →
      i < j →
      j ≤ n / 2 →
      (n, i, j) ∉ E →
      ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (Nat.choose n i) (Nat.choose n j) := by
  sorry

end Erdos699

findings.description: The initial `∃ E : Finset (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ)` asserts that there are globally only finitely many exceptional triples, including those with i = 2 or i = 3. The source's wording is less precise: it says 'except in a few special cases', then discusses parametric exceptional cases at i = 2 and i = 3, and specifically singles out i ≥ 4 for the expectation of only a few incidental counterexamples. Thus the Lean statement imposes a substantive finiteness assertion on the small-index cases that the sources inspected do not clearly support. This is a modelling ambiguity, not a demonstrated disproof: the examples in the paper alone do not establish infinitely many exceptions.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Szekeres, 'Some number theoretic problems on binomial coefficients', Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), pp. 97–98, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-46.pdf: equation (5) is conjectured to hold 'except in a few special cases'. The discussion considers i = 2 with n = 2^r = pq + 1 (including n = 16 and 2048), then i = 3 with numbers 3^r + 1, and says: 'For i ≥ 4 there should only be a few incidental counterexamples to (5).' https://www.erdosproblems.com/699 likewise says 'a few special cases', rather than explicitly asserting finitely many triples.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended exceptional-set claim. A conservative precise variant is to restrict the finite-exception statement to `4 ≤ i`, documenting the i = 2 and i = 3 cases separately. Retaining `1 ≤ i` should be supported by a source explicitly conjecturing global finiteness; if exceptional families are intended instead, encode their exclusion rather than an arbitrary finite set of triples.

could_not_verify: Erdos699.erdos_szekeres_strengthening: Could not conclusively settle whether the source's qualitative 'few special cases' means finitely many triples globally or allows exceptional parametric families at i = 2 and i = 3. This is the modelling concern recorded above; no claim of infinitely many exceptions has been established in this review.
review.notes: No definite mathematical mismatch was found in `Erdos699.sylvester_schur` or `Erdos699.erdos_699`. Lean checks confirmed that natural division encodes the half-row bound correctly, admissible binomial coefficients are positive, gcd divisibility means common divisibility, and the finite-exception formulation is equivalent to finiteness of the failure set. Computations found no counterexample to the main statement for n ≤ 120 and reproduced the source's exceptional gcd values, including gcd(C(2048,2), C(2048,713)) = 1024. The linked formal proof has the identical theorem statement and no explicit placeholders; after compatibility-only edits confined to a scratch copy, its axioms were [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. All experiments were placed in /workspace/review; the reviewed file was not changed.
